name: Central African Republic

findings.local_actor: Government of the Central African Republic (Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications)
findings.builder: Burotop Iris (works), supervised by Taihan group
findings.financier: African Development Bank and European Union
findings.summary: The CAR segment of the Central African Backbone fibre network, about 935 km linking Bangui to Cameroon and Congo-Brazzaville, was handed to the government in February 2023 after AfDB/EU co-financing; Ecofin reports it operational since 2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: under the equipment rule the controller is the transmission-equipment vendor, which no opened source names. Builder nationality not stated; Taihan is presumably the Korean cable maker, but that is unconfirmed. Values given as EUR 33.3m (2018) and CFA 22bn (about US$36m per We Are Tech); not converted here. Length variously 1,100 km (plan), 935 km and about 900 km. Operator PPP for capacity sales not yet selected in 2023.

findings.local_actor: Government of the Central African Republic
findings.summary: After a convention with the government signed 18 December 2025, Starlink launched commercial satellite internet in the CAR in March 2026; the government plans to use it for prefectural administration, rural schools and telemedicine.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 (authorisation in force and service launched) rather than 5, as subscriber scale is unknown. On 29 April 2026 the government suspended roaming kits bought abroad over homologation and user-traceability rules; that is enforcement of the licensing regime, not a reversal, so not coded separately. Afrique IT News coded S2 as specialist tech press; if treated as S3 this falls to uncorroborated.

findings.summary: US firm GreenLine Technologies signed an MoU in September 2025 to take over the dormant state operator SOCATEL with a planned US$150m investment, including a Tier III data centre and national connectivity; definitive agreements were still pending in July 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us on the assumption GreenLine would own and operate SOCATEL and the data centre after takeover; equipment vendors unknown. Tier 1: implementation launch and joint steering committee on 16 July 2026, but takeover agreements not finalised. MoU signed in Casablanca. SOCATEL ceased operations in 2019; earlier revival attempts failed (see CAF-005).

findings.controller: Government of the Central African Republic (public administration)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications
findings.summary: A May 2026 working meeting between the digital ministry and a Huawei delegation discussed a China-backed administration-modernisation programme: a Tier III national data centre, a five-site microwave government network, IP telephony and an eLTE radio network for security forces.
findings.analyst_inference: Detail comes from an Agence Ecofin article (27 May 2026) seen only as a republication on osiris.sn, which is not cited; the Digital Business Africa page body did not load. Tier 1: discussion only, no signed agreement, value or financier. Data centre coded domestic as a state facility with Huawei as presumed builder/equipment supplier; the network and eLTE components would be prc under the equipment rule (CAF-005 bundle).

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications; defence and security forces
findings.summary: The same proposed Huawei programme includes a dedicated microwave network with five radio sites interconnecting ministries and an eLTE radio transmission network for the armed forces, police and gendarmerie.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei as equipment vendor, so prc. Tier 1: working-meeting stage only. Described as following commitments from a Touadera-China meeting; financing (possibly China Eximbank) not stated and should not be assumed.

findings.financier: Government of the Central African Republic (EUR 20m committed)
findings.reversal_of: 2020 agreement for French firm Global Technologies to rehabilitate SOCATEL's microwave network
findings.summary: In November 2020 the government signed with French firm Global Technologies to repair SOCATEL's ageing microwave network; EcoMatin later reported the project abandoned because the state could not raise the roughly EUR 20m needed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Global Technologies would have operated the rehabilitation; the underlying equipment vendor is unknown. Reversal date unknown, hence null. The abandonment rests on EcoMatin alone; Developing Telecoms says only that little is known of progress. Reason commercial (financing failure), so it does not move the map.
